newsitem.title: CHINA: China says rural health care basically unchanged.
newsitem.headline: China says rural health care basically unchanged.

text.p: China's President Jiang Zemin has called for renewed efforts to improve rural health care, saying there had been no fundamental change in farmers' health care conditions, official media said on Tuesday.
Although China had set up a basic rural health care network, much work needed to be done, the People's Daily quoted Jiang as telling a health care conference in Beijing on Monday.
"On the whole, there has been no fundamental change with regards to the weak rural health care situation," the newspaper quoted Jiang as saying.
Jiang also warned health care workers to pay more attention to professional ethics and resist the temptations offered by economic reform.
Health workers should renew efforts at providing rural areas with basic health care and to narrow the health care gap between more developed urban areas and the lagging countryside, he said.
"Farmers cannot afford to see doctors and disease is a major barrier that prevents farmers from overcoming poverty and becoming wealthy," Jiang said.
The improved health of farmers would help in implementing economic and social reforms in rural areas and would lead to improved economic performance, he said.

Nearly two decades of market-oriented economic reform would inevitably have some negative effects on the medical profession, Jiang said, adding that doctors needed to emulate communist values of self-sacrifice and serving the people.

"Professional ethics of medical personnel face new tests and we must find a way to help them resist unhealthy tendencies and increase their awareness of the need to serve the people whole-heartedly," he said.
Many patients complain that doctors, whose salaries are often no more than that of an average factory worker, demand "red envelopes", or bribes, for operations.
Three-fourths of China's population of 1.2 billion live in the countryside and health care conditions are poor in impoverished regions.
